newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, possibly losing edge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, possibly losing edge.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds, which have outshone Treasuries for much of the past six weeks, were flat in early trade on Friday, and some traders said munis now looked less likely to outperform Treasuries in rising markets.

While municipals still were expected to resist any downward pressure more than Treasuries, mainly due to the lack of supply of new issues, traders said that recent price gains achieved by municipal bonds over the past two weeks or so have sliced into retail interest by cutting yields.

"It's not because the technical picture has changed, that's still in favor of higher cash prices," a trader said. "It's just in terms of retail interest," he said, explaining that wirehouses were seeing less buying interest from clients.
Further, reports that municipal bond funds have seen over $900 million drained for redemptions also cut away at the market's ability to keep outperforming Treasuries.
Yet new supplies remain slim, with next week's calender predicted at only around $1.8 billion--the smallest amount seen since early February, when supplies dipped to under $1.6 billion.

Next week's negoitated calender includes a $150 million sale of revenue bonds by the Massachusetts Housing Finance Authority, through Bear, Stearns and Co, and an over $92 million sale by the New York State Dormitory Authority, through Merrill Lynch.
On the competitive side, New York City plans to sell $200 million of general obligation bonds, followed by Virginia, which was expected to sell almost $151 million of its general obligations.
In the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List was pegged at $1.2 billion, little changed.

Cleveland, Ohio, Certificates of Participation Cleveland Stadium Project of 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were offered at 5.63 percent, NET, down six points. And Jefferson County, Alabama Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 99-1/4, unchanged.
June municipal bond futures rose 10 ticks to 116-31/32, while June Treasury bond futures climbed 15 ticks to 109-24/32. The MOB spread stood at 231 ticks, down slightly.
